newsitem.title: USA: US FCC provides new spectrum for satellite service.
newsitem.headline: US FCC provides new spectrum for satellite service.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Thursday allocated an additional 250 megahertz of "uplink" spectrum to the Fixed-Satellite Service on a co-primary basis.
The FSS is a radiocommunication service between earth stations at a specified fixed point -- or between any fixed point within specified areas -- and one or more satellites.
The FCC said the additional spectrum will accommodate the growing demand for fixed-satellite services and will provide satellite operators with greater flexibility in the design of their systems.
The decision is based on the growing deman for FSS in the Ku-band portion of the airwaves, the FCC said.
It said the more than 100 satellites are palnned worldwide would make use of the 13.75-14.0 GHz band.
The location of some of these systems are well suited for service to and from the United States, the FCC added.

In addition, the agency said the location "would further the competiveness of U.S. satellite operators in domestic and international markets and would provide more open and competetive markets for consumers."
